# Current state — jpegxl-rs

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Terms

_(none)_

## Constraints

### Correctness order: conformance before performance

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.correctness-before-speed/1` · scope `all` · topic `correctness-order`

Work proceeds in this order of priority: conformance, resource safety, memory
ownership, scalar performance, parallelism, SIMD, then encoder quality search.

### Correctness is measured by pixels, not byte-parity with libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.correctness-metrics/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/**"` · topic `correctness-metrics`

Decoder success is not lossless correctness. Conformance compares parse success,
dimensions, bit depth, color interpretation, frame count, an exact pixel hash for
lossless paths, and peak error plus RMSE for conforming lossy paths. Byte-for-byte
parity with libjxl is not a general target.

### The decoder enforces explicit resource limits

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.decoder-resource-limits/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `resource-limits`

The decoder enforces explicit, configurable upper bounds and validates all TOC
ranges before allocating or launching workers.

### Start forbidding unsafe; add SIMD unsafe only with a local contract

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.forbid-unsafe-by-default/1` · scope `all` · topic `unsafe-policy`

Crates start with forbid(unsafe_code). Unsafe SIMD is added only after profiles show
a concrete bottleneck and only where the safety contract is local and documented.

### No runtime dependency on libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.no-libjxl-runtime-dep/1` · scope `all` · topic `no-libjxl-dep`

The shipped library has no runtime dependency on libjxl or any C JPEG XL codec.
External decoders are invoked only as separate processes by the conformance harness.

### Parsers use checked arithmetic and never panic on bad input

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.no-panic-checked-arith/1` · scope `all` · topic `no-panic`

Every parser operation uses checked arithmetic and enforces resource limits.
Invalid or unsupported syntax returns a typed error; it never panics and never
silently substitutes defaults.

## Policies

### Clean-room: no architectural port of libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.clean-room-boundary/1` · scope `all` · topic `clean-room`

This is a native, standard-first Rust implementation. Implement from ISO/IEC 18181
and legitimately obtained specifications, never by porting libjxl architecture or
code. libjxl and other decoders are validation oracles only.

### Test count is not confidence; unknown coverage stays unknown

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.coverage-honesty/1` · scope `all` · topic `coverage-honesty`

Do not equate the number of tests with confidence, and do not claim conformance
coverage that has not been demonstrated against the corpus. Unknown profile and
feature coverage must be recorded as unknown, not assumed.

### E.4.4 ICC tag dictionary has 17 entries; use the LaTeX

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.e44-tag-dictionary/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `e44-tag-dictionary`

The E.4.4 tag dictionary has 17 entries (tagcode range 4..=20), including bTRC and
dmda. part1.md truncates it to 15 (OCR dropped those two). Use the LaTeX source;
confirmed by byte-exact fixtures.

### Encoder heuristics are not normative; keep them out of the syntax model

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.encoder-analysis-separate/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `encoder-analysis`

Keep encoder analysis (predictor evaluation, MA-tree construction, context
clustering, palette/RCT/Squeeze selection, LZ77 matching, block/quant search)
separate from the decoder-visible syntax model. A decoder-visible MaTree is
normative data; the algorithm that discovers it is not. Do not let an encoder
heuristic become a decoder requirement.

### EXPERIMENT_CLAMP_SYMMETRIC = false is not a loosened check

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.h52-clamp-asymmetric/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `h52-clamp`

Keep the asymmetric H.5.2 clamp (EXPERIMENT_CLAMP_SYMMETRIC = false). Do not
restore the printed symmetric clamp "to match the spec".

### jpxl bench isolates Modular and VarDCT encode paths

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.jpxl-bench-entry-points/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `jpxl-bench-entry-points`

Profile Modular and VarDCT separately. The CLI encode path is Modular only; a
flamegraph of jpxl encode does not describe VarDCT.

Measurement modes via release jpxl bench:
- modular: Modular lossless (MA search, residuals, LZ77, entropy, bit writing)
- vardct-fixed: VarDCT fixed quantizer (transform selection, transforms, CfL,
  quantize, emit; no rate-loop multiplication)
- vardct-rate: VarDCT target rate (full exact-price rate loop)
- vardct-probe: one predetermined quantizer plan+emit

Optional --input path.ppm (8-bit RGB P6) replaces the synthetic RGB pattern.
Output fields: wall_ms_total, wall_ms_median, output_bytes, and an FNV-1a
fingerprint for cross-iteration identity. Promote to a baseline only under
@jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules (crypto hashes of binary and stream,
decode gate, size classes); FNV alone is not enough for promotion.

### modular_16bit_buffers = false for >8-bit encodes is deliberate

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.modular-16bit-buffers/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `modular-16bit-buffers`

For >8-bit encodes, modular_16bit_buffers = false is deliberate: it is a truthful
claim about decoder working buffers (D.3), and its paired consequence is the jxll
level-10 box in container output (Annex M). Do not restore the Table D.3 default.

### Modular residual LZ77 must use H.3 dist_multiplier

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.modular-lz77-dist-multiplier/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"` · topic `modular-lz77-dist`

The residual SymbolDecoder must be given set_dist_multiplier(max_channel_width).
Encode distances as raw = distance + 119 when M > 0 (C.3.3 past the special table),
never raw = distance - 1 as if M = 0. Do not "fix" round-trip failures under full
modular decode by forcing M = 0 on the decoder.

### Correctness gates by optimization change type

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.optimization-correctness-gates/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/**"` · topic `optimization-gates`

Gate each optimization class before merge: bulk bit writer, plan Arc-sharing,
flat coefficient arena, and scratch reuse require byte-identical codestreams;
Rayon section encoding requires byte-identical results across thread counts;
integer SIMD requires scalar-versus-SIMD byte identity; floating DCT
factorization or SIMD requires decode validity plus the declared Contract A or
B; search pruning or approximate prices requires size/quality/target adherence
and an exact final-price gate; LZ77 algorithm changes require byte equality if
tie rules are preserved, otherwise equal or better exact stream size. Validate
with the in-project decoder and libjxl (oracle process). Decode time is not
included in encode timing.

### Pass oracle output format explicitly; do not loosen the PPM parser

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.oracle-output-format/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/**"` · topic `oracle-output-format`

jxl-oxide ignores the output-file extension and writes PNG bytes into any filename.
Pass --output-format explicitly. Do not "fix" a BadMagic PPM parse error by
loosening the PPM parser; the harness rejects PPM-from-jxl-oxide before spawning
(OracleError::UnsupportedFormat).

### Promoted performance baseline rules

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules/1` · scope `path "JPXL/**"` · topic `performance-baseline-rules`

A number is a promoted performance baseline only when all of the following hold;
otherwise it is a scratch or diagnostic measurement and must not be treated as a
baseline claim:

1. Immutable binaries: hash every binary involved; recheck before every timed run
   and reject the run if the hash changed.
2. Pinned inputs: exact image, its hash, dimensions, bit depth, and color encoding.
3. Interleaved A/B, never separate batches; report minimum, median, and dispersion.
4. Correctness gate alongside timing: output bytes and hash, and decoded-pixel
   result. A fast wrong answer is not a datum.
5. Host state: thread count, CPU affinity and policy, load, free memory, swap and
   tmpfs use, competing jobs. Measurements under resource pressure are diagnostics
   only, never baselines.
6. Cache regime stated: cold-cache, warm-cache, and warm-process are distinct;
   never merge them.
7. Size classes: at minimum a small (~4 MP) and a large (≥12 MP) image.
8. Unknown stays unknown: if profiling explains 48% of samples, report 48% and
   label the rest UNKNOWN.

Profile Modular and VarDCT separately. The CLI encode path is Modular-only; a
flamegraph of jpxl encode does not describe VarDCT. On hybrid Intel hosts, prefer
an explicit userspace P-core event (cpu_core/cycles/u) and verify that the folded
period total equals the perf event total before trusting an SVG.

### Prefer the LaTeX and image scans over OCR transcriptions

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.prefer-latex-over-ocr/1` · scope `all` · topic `source-of-truth`

For normative constants and algorithms, prefer the LaTeX transcription and, when in
doubt, the image scan, over OCR-derived markdown (part1.md and similar). Do not
re-transcribe values from a source already known to be corrupted; cite the verified
source in the record that carries the value.

### Keep research metrics and benchmarks out of the codec core

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.research-out-of-core/1` · scope `all` · topic `research-separation`

The codec core carries no research metrics, perceptual scoring, or benchmark
scaffolding (for example Butteraugli belongs to encoder development tooling, not the
decoder). The changelog is not a research database. Durable measurement summaries
and baseline rules live in AKR; full raw run logs and flamegraph artifacts live
under .agent/scratch/ (not pruned by akr build). Frozen experiment writeups may
go in JPXL/docs/experiments/ when a self-contained report is warranted.
JPXL/docs/PERFORMANCE.md is a stub only, not the measurement store.

### The encoder writes RestorationFilter explicitly OFF

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.restoration-filter-off/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `restoration-filter`

The encoder writes RestorationFilter explicitly OFF (gab = false, epf_iters = 0)
rather than relying on the Table J.1 defaults (gab = true, epf_iters = 2), because
those defaults are decoder-side smoothing our decoder does not implement yet. If
external decodes drift while self-roundtrip stays green, look here first.

### When every transcription agrees on nonsense, suspect the pipeline

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.suspect-transcription-pipeline/1` · scope `all` · topic `transcription-pipeline`

When every transcription agrees on nonsense, suspect the transcription pipeline,
not the standard. Escalate to the image scan before claiming a standard defect.

### Pre-optimization encode wall-time ladder (release jpxl bench)

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.preopt-encode-baseline-2026-08-06/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`

On 2026-08-06 a release jpxl (sha256 6886ab9a…f8985b, commit 788a3b4e, rustc 1.97.1)
was timed with jpxl bench on host dk-82y3 (i7-13700H, warm-process, synthetic RGB).
Median wall times (ms): 256² modular 629 / vardct-fixed 164 / vardct-rate 5250;
1024² modular 9872 / fixed 1083 / rate 40859; 2048² modular 31391 / fixed 4238 /
rate 139616 (1 iter). Rate-loop cost is ~25–40× a single fixed quantizer encode at
the same size. Modular is slower than fixed VarDCT on this synthetic input.
Full provenance and raw lines: .agent/scratch/preopt-baseline-2026-08-06.md.
Not a promoted baseline under @jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules: no
≥12 MP class, no decode gate in the timed path, FNV fingerprint not SHA-256,
loadavg was non-idle.

Takeaways for profiling (not claims of optimality): rate-loop multiplicity is the
first VarDCT structural target; fixed ≈ probe unit cost; Modular per-pixel cost on
this synthetic path makes Opt-M tiered planning as important as VarDCT structure;
BitWriter bulk (Opt-B) is already in tree for this ladder.

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.observation.preopt-encode-baseline-2026-08-06/1`

### Pre-opt P-core flamegraphs: ANS/BitWriter modular; HfQuantizer+matrix DCT VarDCT

HOTSPOTS.md, PROVENANCE.md). Capture: release jpxl 6886ab9a…, commit 788a3b4e,
cpu_core/cycles/u @997Hz, dwarf call-graphs, taskset -c 0-5. Stems: modular-1024.v2
(Modular 1024² ×3), vardct-fixed-2048.v2 (VarDCT fixed 2048² ×3),
vardct-rate-1024.v2 (VarDCT rate 1024² ×1 @1 bpp). Modular top leaves: ANS
encode_symbols ~11%, HybridUint tokenize ~6%, BitWriter::write_bits ~4.5%,
residual/MA collection ~5%, palette memcmp ~3%. VarDCT fixed: HfQuantizer::choose
~22%, matrix_pass ~8% (dense DCT32), reconstruct/clamp/bias/dequant ~15% combined.
VarDCT rate multiplies the same HfQuantizer+matrix_pass leaves (choose ~16%) —
multiplicity of plan_at, not a different kernel. Prefer .v2 artifacts; first-pass
cycles:u data was discarded as hybrid-PMU polluted. Recipe in PROVENANCE.md.
Next targets from this data: Opt-V (cut rate-loop re-entry), Opt-D factored scalar
DCT32, Opt-M residual/MA exact-price multiplicity, then entropy/ANS leaf work.

## Assessments

### Encoder static assessment: multiplicity and structure before SIMD

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.encoder-static-optimization/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`

Static review of the encoder (no measured flamegraph on this snapshot) ranks
gains as: (1) bulk BitWriter instead of bit-at-a-time; (2) stop deep-cloning
quantized VarDCT plans; (3) cut rate-loop work that re-plans nearly everything
per probe; (4) factored scalar DCT32 before vectorizing the dense matrix path;
(5) group coefficient arenas instead of per-varblock heap; (6) cache selected
transforms within one probe; (7) tiered Modular MA/residual scoring instead of
exact-encoding dozens of candidates; (8) shape scalar loops for the compiler
before manual SIMD. Profile Modular, VarDCT fixed-quantizer, and VarDCT
target-rate separately. Rankings are source findings, not measured percentages.
